q: Which figure shows a dimmer switch?
n: Figure A is a slide dimmer.

q: Which figure shows a USB outlet?
n: Figure C has USB ports.

q: Which figure shows a range outlet?
n: Figure B is a high-amperage range outlet.

q: Which figure shows a multipurpose outlet?
n: Figure E is a universal (multipurpose) outlet.

q: Which figure shows a pop-up floor outlet?
n: Figure D is a pop-up floor outlet.

q: What electrical component in Figure A houses circuit breakers or fuses to distribute power within a building?
n: Figure A is a panel board.

q: What enclosure in Figure B is used to safely house electrical connections, typically rated by environmental protection standards?
n: Figure B is a NEMA-rated enclosure.

q: What device in Figure C automatically switches a load between two power sources, often used in backup power systems?
n: Per the MST answer key: Automatic transfer switch.

q: What safety device in Figure D protects electrical circuits by stopping the current flow in case of overload or short circuit?
n: Figure D is a circuit breaker.

q: What device in Figure E is designed to quickly cut power to prevent electric shock, typically used in wet areas?
n: Figure E is a GFCI receptacle.

q: What is image 3 that supplies mechanical energy?
n: Item 3 is the engine, the source of mechanical power.

q: What is image 5 that regulates the generator’s voltage output?
n: Per the MST answer key: Voltage Regulator.

q: What is image 6 that produces the electrical output?
n: Per the MST answer key: Alternator.

q: What is an ATS for in an electrical system?
o: A switch used with a standby generator
An emergency switch in fire alarms
A switch for elevators and conveyors
n: It transfers load between utility and generator.

q: When is the Certificate of Electrical Inspection (CEI) issued?
o: Before the utility installs the meter
After the utility installs the meter
Before the Building Official's final inspection
After the Building Official's final inspection
n: The utility needs the CEI before it energizes and meters the service.

q: When a circuit is divided into two or more branches, each branch transmitting part of the current, what is each branch conductor called when taken separately?
n: Per the MST answer key: Parallel.

q: Which of the following appliances does not require an individual branch circuit?
n: Per the MST answer key: Microwave.

q: What is the standard power voltage supplied by MERALCO?
n: Per the MST answer key: 230V.

q: What frequency does MERALCO supply to consumers?
n: The Philippine grid runs at 60 Hz.

q: In a string of bulbs wired in series, what happens if one bulb is removed?
o: Only the bulb before it goes out
Only bulbs after it go out
n: A series circuit has a single path.

q: What device detects ground faults and cuts power immediately to prevent shock?
n: A GFCI trips on leakage current.

q: What are the conductors from a main distribution center to the branch-circuit panels called?
n: Feeders supply panelboards.

q: What resists the flow of electricity?
n: Insulators have high resistance.

q: What conductors run from the service equipment to distribution points in a building?
n: Feeders run between the service and the panels.

q: A valve controls water flow. What does the same job in an electrical circuit?
n: A switch opens and closes the circuit.

q: What is the minimum wire size required for a service drop?
n: Per the MST answer key: 8 mm².

q: What matters most when sizing wire for a circuit?
n: Wire must carry the load current safely.

q: Power was cut but restored right away by standby generators. What switched the source automatically?
n: An ATS starts and transfers to the generator.

q: What do banks typically use to ensure a smooth transition to emergency power during an outage?
n: Per the answer key, an automatic transfer switch (ATS) shifts the load to the generator.

q: What is the main function of an automatic transfer switch?
o: Switching automatically from the utility to a standby generator
n: It senses outage and transfers load.

q: What is the main purpose of a UPS?
o: Temporary power during outages or until a generator starts
n: Batteries carry the load through the gap.

q: In manual emergency switching, what device connects the load to the alternate source?
n: MTS is a manual transfer switch.

q: THHN wire is used for 600 V AC distribution in dry and damp locations. THHN stands for:
n: T-HH-N: thermoplastic, high heat, nylon.

q: THWN stands for:
n: T-H-W-N: thermoplastic, heat, water, nylon.

q: Why do THHN and THWN wires have a nylon jacket?
n: Nylon resists abrasion when pulled through conduit.

q: What color is a ground wire in residential wiring?
n: Green (or green-yellow) or bare marks grounding.

q: What is conduit for?
n: Conduit encloses and protects conductors.

q: What nominal voltage and frequency are used in the Philippines?
n: Supply is 230 V nominal (often called 220 V) at 60 Hz.

q: Which is a brand of electrical wire?
n: Phelps Dodge is a major wire maker.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of a blender?
n: Per the MST answer key: 1000-500.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of an electric fan?
n: Per the MST answer key: 100.

q: What is the typical power consumption (in watts per hour) of a portable fan?
n: Per the MST answer key: 100-10.
